props.name: accept
props.description: The file types to take, in the `accept` attribute's syntax, such as `"image/*,.pdf"`. The picker receives it as it is, and every source, a pick, a drop or a paste, ends in the same check: a file that fails it reaches `onReject` with `"type"`.

props.name: capture
props.description: Asks a phone to capture new media with the front (`"user"`) or back (`"environment"`) camera.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts: a `FileUpload.Dropzone` for drops, a `FileUpload.Trigger` that opens the picker, and a `FileUpload.Description` of what the Root takes. Without a Dropzone, the Trigger and the Description are a plain picker. A paste adds its files while focus is anywhere inside the Root, such as on the Trigger, and a text field inside the Root keeps its own paste. While any Root is mounted, a file dropped outside every Dropzone does nothing, so a missed drop never opens the file in the tab. A custom part inside the Root reads `useFileUpload()`: `actions.open()` opens the picker from a click or another user gesture, and `actions.add(files)` sends files from another source through the same check as a pick.

props.name: directory
props.description: The picker selects folders, and a dropped folder expands into the files inside it, at any depth. Each file's `webkitRelativePath` holds its path inside the folder, such as `photos/2024/meter.jpg`, for a dropped folder as for a picked one. While it is off, a dropped folder reaches `onReject` with `"directory"`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Ignores every source, and disables each `FileUpload.Trigger`. An enclosing disabled `Field.Root` or `Field.Set` disables the Root as well.

props.name: files
props.description: The files a native form posts, which the parent owns. The Root never changes the list. Add each pick from `onSelect`, and remove files from your own UI, which removes them from the post. A rejected pick, or one the parent does not add, never changes what is posted. The picker stays empty between picks, so picking a file that is already posted still reaches `onSelect`. A native form reset, including the one React runs after a form action, leaves the list and the post as they are. Without a `name`, the files post only under an enclosing `Field.Root`'s `name`, and without `files` the Root posts nothing.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Takes more than one file. Without it, a pick, drop or paste in which more than one file passes `accept` rejects each of those with `"count"`. `accept` is checked first, so a file that fails it is rejected with `"type"` and never counts.

props.name: name
props.description: The name `files` post under with a native form submit or `new FormData(form)`. It needs `files`, so `name` without `files` is a type error. An enclosing `Field.Root`'s `name` takes its place, as it does for Base UI's controls. The Root writes `files` into a hidden input of its own, apart from the picker, so the post carries exactly that list. An empty list posts one empty entry, as a native file input with no selection does. A disabled Root posts nothing.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Receives the files and folders that did not pass, with the reason for each: `"type"` for a file that fails `accept`, `"count"` for each passing file when a Root without `multiple` gets more than one, `"directory"` for a folder while `directory` is off, and `"unreadable"` for a file in a dropped folder that the browser could not read. For one pick, drop or paste, it runs right after `onSelect`, in the same task. Show the rejections in words, such as in an `Alert`, which announces itself.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Receives the files that passed `accept` and the count rule, in a fresh array for each call, which is yours to keep. The Root checks only `accept` and `multiple`. Check limits of your own, such as a file count or a size, here before you keep a file.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: required
props.description: Requires at least one file in `files` before a form submits. An empty or undefined `files` counts as no file, as a native file input with no selection does, and a native form's submit stops and moves focus to the first enabled `FileUpload.Trigger`. Inside a `Field.Root`, the Trigger is the Field's control and `files` its value. The Field validates the files as its `validationMode` says, on the Trigger's blur in `onBlur` mode, and on a Base UI `Form` submit. With none, it turns invalid with `valueMissing`, so `Field.Error match="valueMissing"` describes the Trigger and marks it `aria-invalid`, and a `Form` focuses it. Adding a file clears the error, and opening the picker validates nothing. `onFormSubmit` receives the files under the Field's `name`. A disabled Root is never required.

props.name: children
props.description: The zone's content. Keep a `FileUpload.Trigger` inside for the keyboard: a drop and a click on the zone's empty surface, which opens the picker too, work by pointer only. While a file drag that could pass is over the zone, it sets `data-drop-target`, which turns its dashed border solid on the soft primary fill. When the drop is certain to fail, because a single-file Root gets several files whose types pass `accept` or every file's type misses `accept`, the drag shows the not-allowed cursor and the zone stays as it is. Safari hides the files until the drop, so there the check waits for the drop.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The ids that describe the button. They come first, then, inside a `Field.Root`, the Field's `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` in the Field's order, then each mounted `FileUpload.Description`.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Marks the button invalid. Unset, an invalid Field marks it `aria-invalid` while it is enabled. While it is set, the Trigger paints the shared invalid border and ring, the one invalid face of the FileUpload, so an enclosing `FileUpload.Dropzone` keeps its dashed border.

props.name: children
props.description: The button's label, which names it. Keep a Trigger in every FileUpload: a Dropzone's drop and click work by pointer only, and the Trigger is the keyboard path to the picker. Inside a `Field.Root`, render one Trigger; the Field's label, description and error belong to it. `Field.Label` points at it, so a click on the label opens the picker, and the label follows the Trigger's own text in its name, as in "Choose file Meter photo". Its own `aria-labelledby` replaces that name.

props.name: id
props.description: The button's id. Inside a `Field.Root`, set it here and not on the `render` element, which the label does not follow.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, a `<button type="button">` with the shared focus ring by default. Pass `render={<Button size="sm" />}` for the Fuse button look.

props.name: children
props.description: What the Root takes, such as "Images or PDFs, up to 3 files of 5 MB each". While it is mounted, it describes every `FileUpload.Trigger` in the Root, by the id its element ends up with: the consumer's `id`, one from a `render` element, or a generated one.
